title: Calm VIX: Not Always a Bullish Signal
text: The 15-handle, for example, is not inherently a forecast of quiet. When you start selling in calm environments, there's like a one in three-ish shot that it's likely to have some sort of big repricing within the quarter. So, if we look at the performance here, the spy return over the next 21 days after a 15-handle VIX versus every day, you'll see that it drifts to the left a little bit. And you'll see that it also compresses a little bit. So, one of the things that is good about calm periods is the fact that equity returns also aren't necessarily better, either. And similar left tail. So, for a long equity perspective or just, you know, trying to play the direction, calm VIX doesn't equal upside market over the next 21 trading days.
